summary: René Guénon (1886–1951) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the Robert-Badinter School Complex (1902–1903), Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1904–1906), and the University of Paris (1914–1917).

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz (1923–1959) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University, the University of Vienna, SOAS, and LSE, training under Koppers, Haekel, Bleichsteiner, Tucci, and Rock. He served at Weltmuseum Wien in 1958.
René de Saussure (1868–1943) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (ca. 1893–1895) and held a teaching post at the University of Geneva (ca. 1898–1902).

Richard A. Gard (1914–2007) worked in Buddhist studies. He was a professor at the Institute for the Advanced Study of World Religions and served as director of the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982–1989).

Richard A. Hutch (b. 1945) works in religious studies. He studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He later held posts at Southern Illinois University (ca. 1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (ca. 1978–2010).

Richard A. Rosengarten is a scholar of religious studies. At the University of Chicago, he served as Dean (attested 2008–2012) and as Associate Professor of Religion and Literature, also in the College (attested 2026).
Richard B. Martin (1937–1996) specialized in Indology and Tibetology. He was a professor (attested 1983–1991) and South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003) at the University of Virginia.

Richard Baker (b. 1936) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley, and under Shunryu Suzuki, whom he succeeded. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center (serving as Abbot 1971–1984) and Dharma Sangha.
Richard Barron works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul III.

Richard Bowring (b. 1947) works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge, he held posts at Columbia, Princeton, and Japanese universities, served as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012), and became Emeritus Professor at Cambridge in 1985.

Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, he served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (ca. 1885–1931), and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society.
Richard D. Mann is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003).

Richard D. McBride II specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at UCLA under mentor Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2012).

Richard Delbrueck (1875–1957) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Bonn (ca. 1895–1899). He later held posts at the University of Jena (ca. 1911–1928), Bonn (ca. 1928–1940), and Giessen (ca. 1940–1945).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago by 2004. He has held assistant (attested 2013) and associate professor posts (attested 2026) at Indiana University Bloomington.

Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indology scholar who studied at Kiel University (ca. 1885–1888). He worked at Kiel University Library and Prussian State Library, later serving as head of Göttingen State and University Library (1921–1932).

Richard Foltz (b. 1961) works in Iranian/Central Asian studies, religious studies, and history. Educated at Utah and Harvard, he taught at Kuwait, Brown, Columbia, and Florida, and became Founding Director of the Centre for Iranian Studies at Concordia University.
Richard Fritzsche (b. 1851) was an Indology scholar who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (ca. 1872–1877). He held the post of Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg (attested 1976).

Richard Gombrich (b. 1937) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Oxford under R. C. Zaehner and taught by Obeyesekere and Rahula, he served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College from 1965/1976 to 2004.

Richard Hartshorne (1899–1992) studied at Princeton (ca. 1916–1920) and the University of Chicago (ca. 1920–1924). He held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (ca. 1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1940–1970).
